$comment: DRAFT research data, 2026-09-23. Not wired into policy. Source of truth for docs/research/2026-09-23-dietary-profile-map.md. Medical entries are soft guidance with a clinician note, never diagnosis. Hard avoids only for allergy, celiac, religious, user_rule, or user_confirmed_safety (each rule item confirmed by the user).

evidence_strength.regulatory: Law or labelling rule (FALCPA, CFR) or a drug label.
evidence_strength.strong: Current guideline from a major body, backed by RCTs or consistent data.
evidence_strength.moderate: Guideline advice with weaker data, or consistent observational data.
evidence_strength.limited: Conditional/low-quality evidence; responses differ between people.
evidence_strength.insufficient: No outcome trials; honour only as the user's preference.
evidence_strength.religious_rule: The user's religious practice; the app neither judges nor certifies.

rule_strength.never: Hard. Policy verdict blocked. Requires a permitted hard_basis.
rule_strength.avoid: Soft-strong. Never suggested; logging allowed without nagging.
rule_strength.limit: Soft. Ranking penalty plus optional budget (per meal/day/week).
rule_strength.sometimes: Exception inside a stricter base rule, with a budget or context.

requires_user_confirmation_semantics: true = each hard rule item is confirmed individually by the user before it activates (item-level). false = the profile needs only profile-level confirmation (allergies the user named explicitly are already the user's own statement). A profile is never activated from inference alone.

profile_instance_schema.rule_overrides: [{facet, strength: never|avoid|limit|sometimes|prefer, budget?: {count, per: meal|day|week}, context?: [eating_out, family_meals, holidays, travel], until?: date}]

allergic to nuts.ask: Peanuts, tree nuts, or both? Which ones?

gluten.ask: Is this celiac disease, a wheat allergy, or a sensitivity/choice?

dairy.ask: Is it a milk allergy (reaction to milk protein) or lactose intolerance (stomach upset)?

ambiguous_phrases._rule: An ambiguous allergy phrase activates the BROADER set (safer) until the user answers; the narrower rule replaces it only after the answer.

precedence: clinician-directed soft targets (e.g., CKD protein cap)

profiles.label: Milk allergy

evidence.note: Major allergen (FALCPA). Avoidance is the standard of care.

citations.ref: FDA. Food Allergies (FALCPA + FASTER Act: 9 major allergens).
FDA. Questions and Answers Regarding Food Allergens, Edition 5 (final guidance, Jan 2025; tree-nut list cut to 12, coconut removed; milk/egg widened to other species).

do: Offer calcium- and vitamin-D-fortified plant milks, calcium-set tofu, canned fish with bones.
Read labels each purchase: casein, whey, ghee, lactalbumin, 'non-dairy' creamers can contain casein.
dont: Treat lactose-free milk as safe: it still contains milk protein.
Treat goat or sheep milk as safe (FDA counts all milk).
profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `contains_dairy` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1). Needs the lactose-free and goat/sheep rubric fix.

options.label: My allergist cleared specific baked-milk foods
options.effect: Only the exact foods/recipes the user lists (per the allergist's plan) are allowed; every other baked good stays blocked.

profiles.label: Egg allergy

evidence.note: Major allergen.

citations.ref: FDA. Food Allergies (FALCPA + FASTER Act: 9 major allergens).
FDA. Questions and Answers Regarding Food Allergens, Edition 5 (final guidance, Jan 2025; tree-nut list cut to 12, coconut removed; milk/egg widened to other species).

do: Suggest egg-free binders (flax 'egg', aquafaba) and egg-free protein swaps.
dont: Assume duck or quail eggs are safe.
Miss hidden egg: mayonnaise, meringue, some pasta, glazes, albumin.
profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `contains_egg` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1).

options.label: My allergist cleared specific baked-egg foods
options.effect: Only the exact foods/recipes the user lists are allowed; other baked goods stay blocked.

profiles.label: Peanut allergy

evidence.note: Major allergen; severe reactions common.

citations.ref: FDA. Food Allergies (FALCPA + FASTER Act: 9 major allergens).
NIAID. Guidelines for Clinicians and Patients for Diagnosis and Management of Food Allergy.

do: Treat 'may contain peanuts' / shared-facility warnings as blocked unless the user relaxes it.
dont: Suggest satay, many Asian and African sauces, or mixed nuts without label evidence.
profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `contains_peanut` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1).

profiles.label: Tree-nut allergy

evidence.note: Major allergen. FDA's 2025 list has 12 tree nuts; coconut no longer counts.

citations.ref: FDA. Food Allergies (FALCPA + FASTER Act: 9 major allergens).
FDA. Questions and Answers Regarding Food Allergens, Edition 5 (final guidance, Jan 2025; tree-nut list cut to 12, coconut removed; milk/egg widened to other species).

do: Ask which nuts: many people react to only some; store named nuts via contains_allergen:<name> if narrower.
dont: Assume coconut, nutmeg or water chestnut are tree nuts (they are not); a coconut allergy needs its own named rule.
profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `contains_tree_nut` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1).

profiles.label: Fish allergy

evidence.note: Major allergen.

citations.ref: FDA. Food Allergies (FALCPA + FASTER Act: 9 major allergens).

do: Watch fish sauce, Worcestershire, Caesar dressing, some imitation crab (surimi).
dont: Block shellfish unless the user also names it.
profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `contains_finfish` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1). Until contains_finfish exists, fish_seafood is the (over-inclusive) fallback.

profiles.label: Crustacean shellfish allergy

evidence.note: Major allergen (crustaceans only in US law).

citations.ref: FDA. Food Allergies (FALCPA + FASTER Act: 9 major allergens).
EU Regulation 1169/2011, Annex II (14 allergens incl. mustard, celery, lupin, molluscs, sulphites).

do: Ask whether molluscs (clams, oysters, squid) are also a problem; add allergy_mollusc if yes.
dont: Rely on US labels for molluscs: they are not a declared US allergen.
profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `crustacean_shellfish` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1). Fallback: existing shellfish facet (includes molluscs).

profiles.label: Mollusc allergy

evidence.note: EU Annex II allergen; not a US major allergen, so label evidence is weaker.

citations.ref: EU Regulation 1169/2011, Annex II (14 allergens incl. mustard, celery, lupin, molluscs, sulphites).

profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `mollusc` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1).

profiles.label: Wheat allergy

evidence.note: Major allergen. Different from celiac disease.

citations.ref: FDA. Food Allergies (FALCPA + FASTER Act: 9 major allergens).

do: Allow barley, rye and oats unless the allergist says otherwise.
dont: Treat 'gluten-free' as proof of wheat-free (wheat starch can be gluten-free-processed); check the wheat declaration.
profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `contains_wheat` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1). Fallback: contains_gluten (over-inclusive).

profiles.label: Soy allergy

evidence.note: Major allergen.

citations.ref: FDA. Food Allergies (FALCPA + FASTER Act: 9 major allergens).

profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `contains_soy` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1).

options.label: My allergist said highly refined soy oil / soy lecithin is fine

profiles.label: Sesame allergy

evidence.note: 9th major allergen since the FASTER Act (2023).

citations.ref: FDA. Food Allergies (FALCPA + FASTER Act: 9 major allergens).

dont: Trust older labels or bakery items: some makers added sesame on purpose after the FASTER Act.
profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `contains_sesame` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1).

profiles.label: Other named allergy (mustard, celery, lupin, corn, kiwi, coconut, buckwheat, etc.)

evidence.note: EU Annex II covers mustard, celery, lupin, sulphites; others are individual.

citations.ref: EU Regulation 1169/2011, Annex II (14 allergens incl. mustard, celery, lupin, molluscs, sulphites).
NIAID. Guidelines for Clinicians and Patients for Diagnosis and Management of Food Allergy.

do: Store the user's exact word; confirm spelling; show it on every blocked card.
profiles.jev_design: Parametric noul contains_allergen:<name>, cached per (food revision, name). Floor precedence like the 9 majors.

profiles.label: Alpha-gal syndrome (mammalian meat allergy)

evidence.note: CDC: avoid mammalian meat; some people also react to dairy, mammalian gelatin and other mammal products. Fish gelatin is not a mammal product; gelatin of unstated source is 'unverified'.

citations.ref: CDC. About Alpha-gal Syndrome.
CDC. Products that may contain alpha-gal (mammalian meat, gelatin, dairy; fish gelatin is not a mammal product).

do: Offer poultry, fish, eggs and plant proteins.
dont: Assume poultry is a problem; it is not mammalian.
profiles.jev_design: noul red_meat + mammalian_derived; choice gelatin_source (pork/beef -> blocked, fish/plant -> allowed, unstated -> unverified).

profiles.label: Sulfite sensitivity

evidence.note: FDA requires declaration at >=10 ppm; reactions mostly in people with asthma.

citations.ref: 21 CFR 101.100(a)(4): sulfites >=10 ppm must be declared.
EU Regulation 1169/2011, Annex II (14 allergens incl. mustard, celery, lupin, molluscs, sulphites).

do: Flag wine, dried fruit, bottled lemon juice, some pickles and shrimp.
profiles.jev_design: Parametric allergen noul with name 'sulfites (sulphites, sodium metabisulfite)'.

profiles.label: Oral allergy syndrome (pollen-food)
synonyms: my mouth itches with raw apples

evidence.note: Usually mouth symptoms from the raw food, but systemic reactions including anaphylaxis occur (ACAAI). Cooking often denatures the protein; tolerance is individual.

citations.ref: ACAAI. Pollen Food Allergy Syndrome (systemic reactions possible).
NIAID. Guidelines for Clinicians and Patients for Diagnosis and Management of Food Allergy.

do: Ask what reaction the user had; any throat, breathing or whole-body symptom -> keep all forms blocked and suggest an allergist.
dont: Allow the cooked form unless the user confirms their allergist said so.
profiles.jev_design: Parametric allergen template (global list) or deterministic match per named food; all forms hard by default; cooked forms allowed only with the allergist option.

options.label: My allergist said cooked/canned forms are fine
options.effect: cooked forms allowed; raw stays blocked

profiles.label: Celiac disease
synonyms: I can't have gluten at all

evidence.note: Lifelong strict gluten-free diet is the only treatment; FDA 'gluten-free' <20 ppm.

citations.ref: NIDDK. Eating, Diet, & Nutrition for Celiac Disease.
FDA. Gluten-Free Labeling of Foods (<20 ppm).
FDA. Questions and Answers: Gluten-Free Food Labeling Final Rule.

do: Processed or restaurant food clears only with a gluten-free claim/certification; otherwise 'unverified'.
Oats only if labelled gluten-free.
Count cross-contact warnings as blocked.
dont: Treat barley, rye, malt, brewer's yeast or ordinary oats as safe.
Suggest restaurant fried foods from shared fryers without a caveat.
profiles.jev_design: Floor rule. Deterministic allergen tags first; Jev noul `contains_gluten` on food state only, threshold tuned for recall (a false 'absent' can harm). Outcome 'unknown' = 'Check the label', never suggested (Phase 13 §4.1). Needs the oats/brewer's-yeast rubric fix.

profiles.label: Non-celiac gluten/wheat sensitivity

evidence.note: Diagnosis by exclusion; many symptoms track fructans, not gluten.

citations.ref: Catassi C et al. Diagnosis of NCGS: the Salerno Experts' Criteria. Nutrients 2015. doi:10.3390/nu7064966
Lacy BE et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Management of IBS. Am J Gastroenterol 2021. doi:10.14309/ajg.0000000000001036

do: Suggest the user asks their doctor about celiac testing BEFORE cutting gluten (testing needs gluten in the diet).
dont: Require cross-contact avoidance unless the user asks.
profiles.jev_design: Same facets as celiac; soft by default.

options.label: Treat gluten as a strict rule for me

profiles.label: Lactose intolerance

evidence.note: NIDDK: many people tolerate some lactose (often up to ~12 g at once); hard cheese and yogurt are usually tolerated.

citations.ref: NIDDK. Eating, Diet, & Nutrition for Lactose Intolerance.

do: Rank lactose-free milk, hard cheeses and yogurt as fine.
Keep calcium up.
dont: Block all dairy: this is not an allergy.
Use the contains_dairy facet for this profile.
profiles.jev_design: score high_lactose (3 levels); code limits 'high' items per meal, not all dairy.

profiles.label: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE)

evidence.note: ACG 2025: elimination diets (e.g., dairy-first or multi-food) are a treatment option, with endoscopic monitoring and planned reintroduction. Not an IgE allergy.

citations.ref: ACG Clinical Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Eosinophilic Esophagitis. Am J Gastroenterol 2025. doi:10.14309/ajg.0000000000003194

do: Store exactly the foods the GI team eliminated (often dairy, wheat, egg, soy); track the phase.
dont: Treat EoE eliminations as allergy floor rules with cross-contact blocking unless the team says so.
Start an elimination diet on the app's initiative.
profiles.jev_design: Global allergen facets (contains_dairy, contains_wheat, contains_egg, contains_soy) reused; policy basis user_confirmed_safety.

time_window.type: elimination phase then reintroduction, set by the GI team

evidence.note: Overlaps with IBS; hereditary fructose intolerance is a different, rare, clinician-managed disease.

citations.ref: Monash University. About FODMAPs and IBS (3-phase low-FODMAP diet).

profiles.label: Histamine intolerance (self-reported)

evidence.note: Diagnosis is not standardised; food histamine lists disagree.

citations.ref: Comas-Basté O et al. Histamine Intolerance: The Current State of the Art. Biomolecules 2020. doi:10.3390/biom10081181

do: Use the user's own named foods only.
dont: Impose a long generic list.
profiles.jev_design: Parametric contains_ingredient per user-named trigger; tyramine_rich is NOT a histamine proxy.

evidence.note: Fava beans can trigger haemolysis in G6PD deficiency.

citations.ref: MedlinePlus Genetics. G6PD deficiency (fava beans trigger hemolysis).

profiles.label: Phenylketonuria (PKU)

target_modifiers.meal_planner: DISABLED - no generated plans or food ideas; logging only
target_modifiers.protein_and_phe: the metabolic clinic's phenylalanine prescription and medical-food regimen only

evidence.note: Aspartame labels must warn phenylketonurics. The whole diet is managed by a metabolic clinic.

citations.ref: 21 CFR 172.804: aspartame label statement 'Phenylketonurics: contains phenylalanine'.
MedlinePlus Genetics. Phenylketonuria.
Smith WE et al. PAH deficiency diagnosis and management: 2023 ACMG evidence-based guideline. Genet Med 2025. doi:10.1016/j.gim.2024.101289

dont: Set protein targets or generate ordinary macro-based plans, suggestions or 'high-protein' ideas.
profiles.jev_design: noul aspartame. Profile switches off the planner and protein nudges.

profiles.label: IBS / low-FODMAP
synonyms: my dietitian put me on FODMAP

evidence.note: ACG 2021: conditional recommendation for a limited low-FODMAP trial; best with a dietitian. Not a lifelong diet.

citations.ref: Lacy BE et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Management of IBS. Am J Gastroenterol 2021. doi:10.14309/ajg.0000000000001036
Monash University. About FODMAPs and IBS (3-phase low-FODMAP diet).
NIDDK. Eating, Diet, & Nutrition for IBS.

do: Track the phase; after elimination, prompt reintroduction.
Keep only the groups that the user's reintroduction showed are triggers.
dont: Keep all FODMAPs restricted indefinitely.
Present Jev FODMAP tags as lab values (Monash data are the reference).
profiles.jev_design: Existing low_fodmap flag uses category rules for onion_garlic/beans; add 4 subclass nouls + high_lactose score.

phases: reintroduction (one FODMAP group at a time)

profiles.label: Crohn's disease

evidence.note: AGA 2024: Mediterranean diet for most IBD patients; no diet consistently prevents flares. Triggers are individual.

citations.ref: Hashash JG et al. AGA Clinical Practice Update on Diet and Nutritional Therapies in IBD. Gastroenterology 2024;166:521-532. PMID 38276922
Levine A et al. Dietary Guidance From the IOIBD. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2020. doi:10.1016/j.cgh.2020.01.046
Crohn's & Colitis Foundation. Diet and Nutrition.

do: Build the plan from the user's own confirmed triggers (Phase 13 §4.3).
Watch protein and energy intake during flares (malnutrition risk).
dont: Blanket-ban fibre, dairy or gluten.
Comment on symptoms, flares or medications (deflect.ts).
profiles.jev_design: Facets on foods only; the diagnosis never goes to Jev.

options.label: My doctor says I have a narrowing/stricture

profiles.label: Ulcerative colitis

evidence.note: IOIBD 2020: reduce red and processed meat, emulsifiers and dairy fat; increase marine omega-3 from food. Low-quality evidence.

citations.ref: Levine A et al. Dietary Guidance From the IOIBD. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2020. doi:10.1016/j.cgh.2020.01.046
Hashash JG et al. AGA Clinical Practice Update on Diet and Nutritional Therapies in IBD. Gastroenterology 2024;166:521-532. PMID 38276922
Crohn's & Colitis Foundation. Diet and Nutrition.

do: Keep the user's own confirmed avoid rules as the primary layer.
dont: Diagnose flares or advise on medication.

profiles.label: Low-fibre / low-residue diet (doctor-directed, usually temporary)
synonyms: doctor said no fiber for now

evidence.note: Used short-term for flares, strictures or procedure prep; content set by the care team.

citations.ref: Hashash JG et al. AGA Clinical Practice Update on Diet and Nutritional Therapies in IBD. Gastroenterology 2024;166:521-532. PMID 38276922
NIDDK. Eating, Diet, & Nutrition for Diverticular Disease.

do: Ask for an end date and revert automatically.
Follow any written prep sheet the user gives over the app's list.
dont: Leave a temporary directive on indefinitely.

profiles.label: Acid reflux / GERD

evidence.note: ACG 2022: weight loss if overweight and no meals 2-3 h before bed are suggested; avoid only the foods that trigger YOUR symptoms.

citations.ref: Katz PO et al. ACG Clinical Guideline for GERD. Am J Gastroenterol 2022. doi:10.14309/ajg.0000000000001538
NIDDK. Eating, Diet, & Nutrition for GER & GERD.

do: Offer an evening meal-timing nudge.
dont: Ban the whole common-trigger list by default.
profiles.jev_design: Only the user-chosen trigger facets; plus contains_ingredient:<name> for chocolate/mint.

options.label: Pick my triggers
options.effect: user toggles any of: caffeine, coffee_or_tea, alcohol, spicy_hot, high_acid, carbonated, high_fat, fried, chocolate, mint

profiles.label: Diverticulosis / diverticulitis

evidence.note: AGA 2021: high-fibre diet; nuts, seeds and popcorn need NOT be avoided; limit red meat. Acute attacks: follow the clinician's short-term plan.

citations.ref: Peery AF et al. AGA Clinical Practice Update on Medical Management of Colonic Diverticulitis. Gastroenterology 2021. doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2020.09.059
NIDDK. Eating, Diet, & Nutrition for Diverticular Disease.

do: Actively correct the nuts/seeds/popcorn myth if the user raises it.
dont: Block nuts, seeds or popcorn.
profiles.jev_design: No new facet needed beyond high_fiber/whole_grain/red_meat.

profiles.label: Gout / high uric acid

evidence.note: ACR 2020: conditionally limit alcohol, purine intake and high-fructose corn syrup; urate-lowering therapy is the main treatment.

citations.ref: FitzGerald JD et al. 2020 ACR Guideline for the Management of Gout. Arthritis Care Res 2020. doi:10.1002/acr.24180

do: Frame as supportive to medication, not a substitute.
dont: Promise diet alone controls gout.
profiles.jev_design: noul high_purine; beer is caught by alcohol + high_purine.

profiles.label: Type 1 diabetes

target_modifiers.carb_awareness: show carbs per meal; do not compute insulin

evidence.note: ADA SOC 2026: no single macronutrient split; carbohydrate counting matched to insulin; alcohol can cause delayed hypoglycaemia.

citations.ref: American Diabetes Association. Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (Sections 3 and 5). Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1).
Evert AB et al. Nutrition Therapy for Adults With Diabetes or Prediabetes: A Consensus Report. Diabetes Care 2019. doi:10.2337/dci19-0014

do: Show carbohydrate grams clearly.
Remember fast sugar is the TREATMENT for a low: never flag glucose tabs/juice logged for a hypo.
dont: Suggest insulin doses or corrections.
Suggest keto or fasting without the care team (see conflicts).
profiles.jev_design: high_carb_starchy is only a ranking hint; carb grams come from nutrient data.

target_modifiers.skipped_meals_and_fasting: no fasting/IF/Ramadan plan generated without a clinician-approved plan
target_modifiers.alcohol: with food only; lows can be delayed
target_modifiers.hypo_treatment_foods: never flagged when logged for a low

evidence.note: ADA SOC 2026: insulin and insulin secretagogues cause hypoglycaemia; alcohol and missed meals raise the risk.

citations.ref: ADA. 5. Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026. doi:10.2337/dc26-S005
American Diabetes Association. Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (Sections 3 and 5). Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1).

profiles.label: Type 2 diabetes

evidence.note: ADA SOC 2026 / 2019 consensus: several patterns work (Mediterranean, DASH, low-carb, plant-based); cut added sugars and refined grains; water over sugary drinks.

citations.ref: American Diabetes Association. Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (Sections 3 and 5). Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1).
Evert AB et al. Nutrition Therapy for Adults With Diabetes or Prediabetes: A Consensus Report. Diabetes Care 2019. doi:10.2337/dci19-0014

do: Let the user pick a pattern (Mediterranean, low-carb, etc.); layer it.
Ask the treatment question before any fasting, IF or low-carb plan.
dont: Promise remission.
Change medication timing.

options.label: Diabetes treatment
options.effect: insulin/sulfonylurea -> insulin_or_sulfonylurea profile; SGLT2 -> sglt2_inhibitor profile; unanswered or unsure -> treated as high-risk for fasting gates

evidence.note: ADA SOC 2026 Section 3: ~7% weight loss plus activity (DPP) delays progression.

citations.ref: American Diabetes Association. Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (Sections 3 and 5). Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1).

profiles.label: Gestational diabetes

evidence.note: ADA SOC 2026 §15: at least 175 g carbohydrate, 71 g protein, 28 g fibre per day; carbohydrate distribution is individualised.

citations.ref: ADA. 15. Management of Diabetes in Pregnancy: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (>=175 g carbohydrate/day; ketogenic diets not recommended). doi:10.2337/dc26-S015

dont: Set a calorie deficit.
Override the care team's meal plan.
profiles.jev_design: as type2_diabetes; pregnancy profile also applies.

profiles.label: High blood pressure

evidence.note: 2025 AHA/ACC: DASH-style pattern, sodium <2300 moving to <1500 mg, more dietary potassium, less alcohol.

citations.ref: 2025 AHA/ACC multisociety Guideline for High Blood Pressure in Adults. JACC 2025. doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2025.05.007 (sodium <2300 toward <1500 mg; potassium 3500-5000 mg from food unless CKD/K-retaining drugs; K salt substitutes except CKD/K-retaining drugs).
NHLBI. DASH Eating Plan.
AHA. How much sodium should I eat per day? (<=2300 mg, ideal 1500 mg).

do: Use label sodium first; Jev high_sodium only when no label.
dont: Recommend potassium salt substitutes or high-potassium pushes if CKD or ACE-inhibitor/ARB/spironolactone is on the profile.

profiles.label: Heart disease / high LDL cholesterol
synonyms: high triglycerides (clinician may add alcohol/sugar limits)

evidence.note: AHA 2026 dietary guidance (supersedes 2021): healthy weight; plenty of varied vegetables/fruit; whole grains; healthy proteins; unsaturated in place of saturated fat; minimally processed over ultra-processed; minimise added sugars; less sodium; if you don't drink, don't start.

citations.ref: 2026 Dietary Guidance to Improve Cardiovascular Health: AHA Scientific Statement. Circulation 2026. doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001435 (supersedes 2021).

USDA/HHS. Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2025-2030 (released 2026-01-07): protein 1.2-1.6 g/kg/day, sat fat <=10% kcal, sodium <2300 mg (14+), limit highly processed foods and added sugars, no alcohol in pregnancy.

do: Offer swaps (olive oil for butter, fish/beans for processed meat).
dont: Set dietary cholesterol caps as a separate rule (no numeric DGA limit).

profiles.label: Chronic kidney disease (not on dialysis)

target_modifiers.stage_required: ask G1-G5 and dialysis status; no protein change until known
target_modifiers.protein_exceptions: not for metabolically unstable or malnourished users - clinician decides

evidence.note: KDIGO 2024: protein 0.8 g/kg/day for G3-G5, avoid >1.3; sodium <2 g/day; potassium and phosphorus individualised to labs.

citations.ref: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD (protein 0.8 g/kg G3-G5; avoid >1.3; sodium <2 g/day).
Ikizler TA et al. KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD: 2020 Update. Am J Kidney Dis 2020. doi:10.1053/j.ajkd.2020.05.006
NIDDK. Healthy Eating for Adults with Chronic Kidney Disease.
Yasawardene P et al. Nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity following star fruit ingestion: a narrative review. Trans R Soc Trop Med Hyg 2021. PMID 33693950

do: Make star fruit a confirmed hard rule (neurotoxic in kidney failure).
Surface the protein conflict with any muscle-gain goal.
dont: Auto-restrict potassium or phosphorus without the care team.
Push potassium salt substitutes.
profiles.jev_design: Food facets only; protein comes from nutrient data.

options.label: My care team told me to limit potassium
My care team told me to limit phosphorus

profiles.label: Kidney failure on dialysis

evidence.note: KDOQI 2020: protein 1.0-1.2 g/kg/day on maintenance dialysis; fluid, potassium and phosphorus per labs.

citations.ref: Ikizler TA et al. KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD: 2020 Update. Am J Kidney Dis 2020. doi:10.1053/j.ajkd.2020.05.006
Yasawardene P et al. Nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity following star fruit ingestion: a narrative review. Trans R Soc Trop Med Hyg 2021. PMID 33693950

do: Count soups, ice and jelly toward a fluid limit if the team set one.
dont: Apply the non-dialysis 0.8 g/kg protein cap.

options.label: My dialysis team told me to limit potassium
My dialysis team told me to limit phosphorus

profiles.label: Kidney stones (calcium oxalate)

evidence.note: AUA 2014: high fluid, normal dietary calcium, limit sodium and animal protein; oxalate limits only for high urinary oxalate.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain meat from a mammal?

rubric.true: The food contains muscle meat, organ meat, or minced/processed meat from a mammal such as cattle, pig, sheep, lamb, goat, deer, bison, rabbit or horse.
rubric.false: The food contains no mammal meat; poultry, fish, shellfish, eggs, dairy and plant foods alone are false.

new_facets.note: Mammal meat, matching the alpha-gal and IARC 'red meat' scope. Existing pork and beef facets stay as narrower subsets.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food, or does it contain, processed meat?

rubric.true: The food contains meat preserved by curing, salting, smoking, fermenting or added nitrite/nitrate, such as bacon, ham, sausage, hot dog, salami, pepperoni, deli/luncheon meat, corned beef or jerky.
rubric.false: The food contains no cured, smoked, salted or nitrite-preserved meat; fresh unprocessed meat alone is false.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain the flesh of a land animal or bird itself (not only broth, fat, gelatin or flavouring)?

rubric.true: The food contains pieces of meat, poultry, organ meat, or processed meat made from them (e.g., chicken, beef, bacon, sausage, ham).
rubric.false: The food contains no land-animal or bird flesh; foods with only broth/stock, gelatin, lard, meat flavouring, fish, eggs or dairy are false.

new_facets.note: USCCB: broth, gelatin and meat-derived flavourings are technically permitted on abstinence days.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain poultry?

rubric.true: The food contains meat, stock or fat from a domesticated or game bird, such as chicken, turkey, duck, goose or quail.
rubric.false: The food contains no bird meat or bird-derived stock; eggs alone are false.

new_facets.note: Needed to model 'mostly pescatarian but sometimes chicken' as an exception, not a new diet.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain finfish, or does its label warn that it may contain fish?

rubric.true: The food states a finfish or finfish-derived ingredient (e.g., salmon, tuna, cod, anchovy, fish sauce, Worcestershire with anchovy, fish gelatin, fish oil) or carries a fish cross-contact warning.
rubric.false: The food states no finfish ingredient and no fish cross-contact warning; shellfish alone is false.

new_facets.note: FDA major allergen 'fish'. The existing fish_seafood facet mixes fish and shellfish, which over-blocks for a fish-only allergy.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain crustacean shellfish, or does its label warn that it may contain crustaceans?

rubric.true: The food states shrimp, prawn, crab, lobster, crawfish/crayfish, krill or another crustacean ingredient, or carries a crustacean cross-contact warning.
rubric.false: The food states no crustacean ingredient and no crustacean warning; molluscs and finfish alone are false.

new_facets.note: FDA major allergen is crustacean shellfish only; molluscs are not a US major allergen.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain a mollusc?

rubric.true: The food contains a clam, mussel, oyster, scallop, squid/calamari, octopus, snail/escargot, abalone, or an extract/sauce from one (e.g., oyster sauce).
rubric.false: The food contains no mollusc or mollusc-derived ingredient.

new_facets.note: Not declared under US FALCPA, so label evidence is weak; EU Annex II does declare molluscs.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain wheat, or does its label warn that it may contain wheat?

rubric.true: The food states wheat or a wheat species/derivative (e.g., spelt, durum, semolina, farro, einkorn, kamut, bulgur, couscous, seitan, wheat starch) or a wheat cross-contact warning.
rubric.false: The food states no wheat ingredient and no wheat warning; barley, rye and oats alone are false.

new_facets.note: Wheat allergy is not celiac disease: barley and rye are allowed for a wheat allergy but blocked for celiac disease.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain gelatin or collagen from an animal?

rubric.true: The food contains gelatin, collagen, gelatine-based capsules or gummies, aspic, or marshmallow made with animal gelatin.
rubric.false: The food contains no animal gelatin or collagen; agar, pectin, carrageenan and plant gums are false.

new_facets.note: Phase 13 spec §4.2 already names no_gelatin. Presence only; the SOURCE is a separate facet (gelatin_source) because fish or certified halal/kosher gelatin is acceptable for several profiles.

new_facets.jev_question: If this food contains gelatin or collagen, what is its stated source?
new_facets.note: 'unstated source' maps to verdict unverified for alpha-gal, halal, kosher and Hindu rules; certification evidence (halal/kosher mark) is read by code, not Jev.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain an ingredient derived from a mammal other than milk?

rubric.true: The food contains mammal meat, organ, blood, lard, tallow, suet, mammal-derived gelatin or collagen, or mammal stock or broth.
rubric.false: The food contains no mammal-derived ingredient other than dairy; poultry, fish and plant foods are false.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain an insect-derived ingredient?

rubric.true: The food contains carmine/cochineal (E120), shellac/confectioner's glaze, or insects/insect flour.
rubric.false: The food contains no insect-derived ingredient; honey is judged separately.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain honey or another bee product?

rubric.true: The food contains honey, bee pollen, royal jelly or propolis.
rubric.false: The food contains no bee-derived ingredient; beeswax coating on fruit is false.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain animal blood?

rubric.true: The food contains blood, blood sausage/black pudding, blood tofu, or blood plasma.
rubric.false: The food contains no animal blood as an ingredient.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this single dish combine meat or poultry with a dairy ingredient?

rubric.true: The dish contains both land-animal meat or poultry and a milk-derived ingredient (e.g., cheeseburger, chicken alfredo, butter chicken with cream).
rubric.false: The dish does not combine meat or poultry with dairy; fish with dairy is false.

new_facets.note: Meal-level: code also checks across items in one logged meal.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain seafood that fails the kosher sign of having both fins and removable scales?

rubric.true: The food contains shellfish or molluscs, or a fish that lacks fins OR lacks removable (kosher) scales, e.g., catfish, eel, shark, monkfish, sturgeon/caviar, swordfish (disputed), or fish of unknown species (e.g., 'fish sticks', 'seafood mix').
rubric.false: Every fish is named and has both fins and removable scales (e.g., salmon, tuna, cod, tilapia, carp), or there is no seafood.

new_facets.note: Swordfish and sturgeon are disputed; the user's own authority decides.

new_facets.jev_question: How much sodium does one typical serving of this food contain?

levels: Very low: under about 140 mg per serving (e.g., fresh fruit, plain oats).
Moderate: about 140-460 mg per serving (e.g., bread slice, plain cheese).
High: about 460-900 mg per serving (e.g., canned soup cup, deli sandwich).
Very high: over about 900 mg per serving (e.g., instant ramen with seasoning, restaurant entrée with soy sauce).

new_facets.deterministic_first: sodium_mg per serving from label: <=140 low (FDA 'low sodium'), >=460 (20% DV) high
new_facets.note: RANK ONLY. A daily mg limit is enforced only from measured nutrients x logged portion; with missing values the app says the limit cannot be checked.

new_facets.jev_question: How much added sugar does one typical serving of this food contain?

levels: None: no sugar or syrup added (whole fruit, plain milk and plain yogurt are none).
Low: a little added sugar, under about 5 g per serving.
Moderate: about 5-10 g per serving.
High: over about 10 g per serving (e.g., soda, candy, frosted cereal, sweet coffee drink).

new_facets.deterministic_first: added_sugars_g from label: >=10 g (20% DV; DGA 2025 per-meal ceiling) high

new_facets.jev_question: Is this a drink sweetened with added sugar?

rubric.true: The item is a beverage with added sugar or syrup, such as regular soda, sweet tea, lemonade, energy drink, sweetened coffee drink or fruit drink.
rubric.false: The item is not a drink, or is a drink without added sugar (water, plain milk, 100% juice, diet soda, unsweetened tea or coffee).

new_facets.jev_question: How processed is this food, using the NOVA classification?

levels: NOVA 1: unprocessed or minimally processed (fresh, frozen, dried, plain milk, eggs, plain meat).
NOVA 2: processed culinary ingredient (oil, butter, sugar, salt, flour).
NOVA 3: processed food made from NOVA 1 foods plus salt/sugar/oil (canned beans, cheese, fresh bread, cured ham).

NOVA 4: ultra-processed industrial formulation with ingredients rarely used at home (e.g., emulsifiers, flavourings, protein isolates, hydrogenated oils): soda, packaged snacks, instant noodles, reconstituted meat.

new_facets.note: Ingredient text makes this reliable; without it Jev relies on the food name.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food list an emulsifier or thickener additive associated with IBD research?

rubric.true: The ingredients include carrageenan, carboxymethylcellulose (cellulose gum), polysorbate 80, maltodextrin or titanium dioxide.
rubric.false: None of those additives are listed or implied.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food deep-fried or pan-fried in a lot of fat?

rubric.true: The food as eaten is deep-fried or fried in a substantial amount of fat (e.g., fries, fried chicken, tempura, doughnuts, pakora, chips/crisps).
rubric.false: The food is not fried, or only lightly sautéed/stir-fried; baked, grilled, steamed and raw are false.

new_facets.jev_question: How much saturated fat does one typical serving contain?

levels: Low: under about 1 g per serving.
Moderate: about 1-4 g per serving.
High: over about 4 g per serving (e.g., butter, cream sauce, fatty red meat, cheese, coconut oil, pastry).

new_facets.deterministic_first: sat_fat_g from label: >=4 g (20% DV) high

new_facets.jev_question: How much total fat does one typical serving contain relative to its size?

levels: Low fat: under about 3 g per serving.
Moderate.
High fat: over about 15 g per serving or visibly greasy/rich.

new_facets.jev_question: Is the grain in this food mainly refined rather than whole grain?

rubric.true: The main grain ingredient is refined (white flour, white rice, degerminated corn, most pasta, white bread, most crackers).
rubric.false: The food has no grain, or its grain is mainly whole grain (whole wheat, brown rice, oats, quinoa, barley).

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food mainly a whole grain or made mainly with whole grain?

rubric.true: The first grain ingredient is a whole grain (e.g., whole wheat, oats, brown rice, quinoa, barley, whole-grain corn, bulgur).
rubric.false: The food has no grain, or its main grain is refined.

new_facets.jev_question: How much dietary fibre does one typical serving contain?

levels: Low: under about 2 g.
Good source: about 3-5 g.
High: over about 5.6 g (20% DV).

new_facets.jev_question: How much hard-to-digest insoluble fibre or residue does this food leave, as eaten?

levels: Low residue: refined grains, well-cooked peeled vegetables, smooth nut butters, tender meat, eggs.
Moderate residue.
High residue: raw vegetables, skins/peels, seeds, whole nuts, popcorn, dried fruit, corn kernels, tough fibrous cuts.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food a major source of carbohydrate?

rubric.true: The food provides roughly 15 g or more of digestible carbohydrate per typical serving (bread, rice, pasta, potato, cereal, most fruit, sweets, sugary drinks).
rubric.false: The food provides little digestible carbohydrate (meat, fish, eggs, cheese, most non-starchy vegetables, oils, nuts).

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain a cereal grain or pseudo-grain?

rubric.true: The food contains wheat, rice, corn/maize, oats, barley, rye, millet, sorghum, quinoa, buckwheat, amaranth or a flour/starch made from them.
rubric.false: The food contains no grain or grain-derived ingredient.

new_facets.jev_question: How large a blood-glucose load would one typical serving of this food cause?

levels: Low: little digestible carbohydrate, or carbohydrate with fibre/protein/fat that slows absorption (non-starchy vegetables, legumes, nuts, plain yogurt).
Medium.
High: large amounts of quickly absorbed carbohydrate (white bread, white rice, potatoes, sugary drinks, sweets, most breakfast cereals).

new_facets.note: A judgement to rank foods, not an insulin dose input. Never shown as a glycaemic-index number.

new_facets.jev_question: About how much caffeine does one typical serving contain?

levels: None: no caffeine at all (water, herbal tea, milk).
Trace: decaf coffee or decaf tea (about 2-15 mg per cup), small amounts of milk chocolate.
Low: under about 50 mg (e.g., green tea cup, cola can, dark chocolate).
Moderate: about 50-150 mg (e.g., cup of brewed coffee, black tea, espresso shot).
High: over about 150 mg (e.g., large coffee, energy drink, pre-workout).

new_facets.note: RANK/FLAG ONLY. A daily caffeine limit (e.g., pregnancy 200 mg) is summed only from known mg values; unknown items show 'caffeine not known' and the day is never reported as within the limit.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this, or does this contain, coffee or tea from the tea plant?

rubric.true: The item is or contains coffee, espresso, or tea from Camellia sinensis (black, green, white, oolong, matcha, chai made with black tea), including iced and decaf forms and coffee- or tea-flavoured foods that use real coffee/tea.
rubric.false: The item contains no coffee or Camellia sinensis tea; herbal infusions (rooibos, chamomile, peppermint), cola and energy drinks are false.

new_facets.note: LDS guidance names coffee and tea, not caffeine. This facet stops the app from treating caffeine as the rule.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food a rich source of marine omega-3 fats (EPA/DHA)?

rubric.true: The food is or mainly contains oily fish or seafood rich in EPA/DHA (e.g., salmon, sardines, mackerel (Atlantic), herring, trout, anchovies) or algae oil.
rubric.false: The food is not a meaningful source of EPA/DHA; plant ALA sources (flax, chia, walnut) are false here.

new_facets.jev_question: Could this food contain a fish that FDA/EPA list among choices to avoid for mercury?

rubric.true: The food contains king mackerel, marlin, orange roughy, shark, swordfish, tilefish (Gulf of Mexico) or bigeye tuna, OR tuna whose species or product type is not stated (e.g., 'tuna steak', 'ahi', 'sushi tuna', 'seared tuna').
rubric.false: Every fish is named and none is on that list: canned light/skipjack tuna, salmon, cod, shrimp and sardines are false; albacore/yellowfin are false here but are 'Good Choices' limited to 1 serving/week (code applies the limit).

new_facets.jev_question: Is an animal food in this item eaten raw or undercooked?

rubric.true: The item includes raw or undercooked meat, poultry, fish, shellfish or eggs as eaten (e.g., sushi/sashimi, raw oysters, ceviche, steak tartare, rare burger, runny eggs, raw cookie dough, homemade mayo/Caesar dressing).
rubric.false: All animal ingredients are fully cooked or pasteurized, or there are none.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain unpasteurized milk, cheese made from it, or unpasteurized juice/cider?

rubric.true: The food states raw/unpasteurized milk, raw-milk cheese, or unpasteurized juice or cider.
rubric.false: The food is pasteurized or contains none of those; hard cheeses from pasteurized milk are false.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this a food that CDC lists as higher risk for Listeria when eaten as is?

rubric.true: The food is one CDC lists as higher-risk: unheated deli meat, cold cuts, hot dogs or fermented/dry sausage; unheated deli-sliced cheese; premade deli salads; refrigerated pâté or meat spreads; refrigerated smoked fish; any unheated queso fresco-type fresh soft cheese (queso fresco, queso blanco, requesón) EVEN IF made with pasteurized milk; raw-milk cheese, milk, yogurt or ice cream; raw or lightly cooked sprouts; raw enoki mushrooms; cut melon left unrefrigerated.
rubric.false: The food is not in those groups, or the description states it is heated to 165°F / steaming hot, or it is a shelf-stable version (shelf-stable pâté or smoked fish). When preparation is not stated, answer as if unheated.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food high in purines?

rubric.true: The food is or mainly contains organ meat (liver, kidney, sweetbreads), game, anchovies, sardines, herring, mackerel, mussels, scallops, trout, meat extract/gravy, or beer.
rubric.false: The food is not a high-purine food; vegetables, dairy, eggs, grains and most legumes are false.

new_facets.jev_question: How much potassium does one typical serving contain?

levels: Low: under about 200 mg.
Moderate: about 200-400 mg.
High: over about 400 mg (e.g., banana, potato, tomato sauce, beans, oranges, avocado, salt substitute).

new_facets.note: RANK ONLY; renal budgets use measured values or are reported as not checkable.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food list a phosphate additive?

rubric.true: The ingredients include a phosphate or 'phos' additive such as sodium phosphate, phosphoric acid, sodium tripolyphosphate, dicalcium phosphate or sodium aluminum phosphate.
rubric.false: No phosphate additive is listed.

new_facets.note: Inorganic phosphate additives are absorbed far more than natural phosphorus.

new_facets.jev_question: How much phosphorus does one typical serving provide?

levels: Low.
Moderate.
High: dairy-heavy foods, processed cheese, colas, organ meats, foods with phosphate additives.

new_facets.note: RANK ONLY; renal budgets use measured values or are reported as not checkable.

new_facets.jev_question: How much vitamin K1 does one typical serving provide?

levels: Low: under about 20 mcg.
Moderate: about 20-100 mcg (e.g., broccoli side, cabbage).
High: over about 100 mcg (e.g., cooked kale, spinach, collards, turnip greens, Brussels sprouts, natto).

new_facets.jev_question: Is this a high-tyramine food of the kind restricted with MAO inhibitors?

rubric.true: The food is or contains cheese (especially aged), yogurt, pickled or smoked fish (e.g., pickled herring), liver, dry/fermented sausage (salami, pepperoni, Lebanon bologna) or other aged/cured meat, fermented soy (soy sauce, miso, fermented tofu), sauerkraut or kimchi, beer (including alcohol-free and tap beer), wine, yeast extract (Marmite, brewer's yeast), fava/broad bean pods, or protein food that is aged, fermented, pickled, smoked or not fresh.
rubric.false: The food is clearly none of those (e.g., fresh plain meat, fresh fish, eggs, fresh vegetables, grains). Anything aged, fermented, pickled, smoked or of unclear freshness is TRUE.

new_facets.note: For non-selective MAOIs this facet is one layer only: code also matches the drug label's own list (phenelzine, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid) and treats any unknown as 'unverified'. A facet 'absent' never clears a label-listed food.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain grapefruit or a related citrus that interacts with some medicines?

rubric.true: The food contains grapefruit, pomelo, Seville/bitter orange (e.g., marmalade), or grapefruit juice, including blends.
rubric.false: The food contains none of these; sweet orange, lemon, lime and tangerine are false.

new_facets.jev_question: How much lactose does one typical serving contain?

levels: None or trace: lactose-free milk, butter, aged hard cheese (cheddar, parmesan, swiss), non-dairy foods.
Low: under about 5 g (e.g., small yogurt, feta, a splash of milk in coffee).
High: over about 5 g (e.g., glass of milk, ice cream, milkshake, ricotta, cottage cheese in quantity).

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food a significant source of fructans in a typical serving?

rubric.true: The food contains a notable amount of wheat, rye or barley (as a main ingredient), onion, garlic, shallot, leek bulb, inulin/chicory root fibre, or fructo-oligosaccharides.
rubric.false: The food contains none of those in a meaningful amount; garlic-infused oil and spring-onion greens are false.

new_facets.note: Monash lab data are the gold standard; Jev only screens.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food a significant source of galacto-oligosaccharides (GOS)?

rubric.true: The food contains a notable amount of legumes/pulses (beans, chickpeas, lentils, soy beans), cashews, pistachios or soy milk made from whole beans.
rubric.false: The food contains none of those in a meaningful amount; canned rinsed lentils in small serves may still be false.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food a significant source of excess fructose?

rubric.true: The food contains a notable amount of apple, pear, mango, watermelon, honey, agave, high-fructose corn syrup or fruit-juice concentrate.
rubric.false: The food contains none of those in a meaningful amount.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food a significant source of polyols (sugar alcohols)?

rubric.true: The food contains sorbitol, mannitol, xylitol, maltitol or isomalt, or a notable amount of stone fruit (peach, plum, cherry, apricot), mushrooms, cauliflower or avocado.
rubric.false: The food contains none of those in a meaningful amount.

new_facets.jev_question: How spicy-hot (chilli heat) is this food?

levels: Not spicy.
Mild.
Medium: noticeable chilli heat.
Hot: strong chilli heat (e.g., vindaloo, hot wings, ghost-pepper sauce).

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food strongly acidic?

rubric.true: The food is or mainly contains citrus fruit or juice, tomato/tomato sauce, vinegar-based dressing or pickle, or a carbonated soft drink.
rubric.false: The food is not strongly acidic.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this a carbonated drink or a food containing one?

rubric.true: The item is a fizzy drink: soda, sparkling water, beer, sparkling wine, kombucha, carbonated energy drink.
rubric.false: The item is not carbonated.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain a root, bulb or tuber vegetable?

rubric.true: The food contains onion, garlic, potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, turnip, sweet potato, yam, ginger root, turmeric root or another vegetable that grows underground.
rubric.false: The food contains no underground root, bulb or tuber vegetable.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain fava (broad) beans?

rubric.true: The food contains fava/broad beans, ful medames, falafel made with fava beans, or fava bean flour.
rubric.false: The food contains no fava bean; chickpea-only falafel is false.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain aspartame?

rubric.true: The ingredients include aspartame or the label says 'Phenylketonurics: contains phenylalanine'.
rubric.false: No aspartame is listed.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain a non-nutritive or low-calorie sweetener?

rubric.true: The food contains sucralose, aspartame, acesulfame K, saccharin, stevia/steviol glycosides, monk fruit extract, or a sugar alcohol such as erythritol or xylitol.
rubric.false: The food contains no such sweetener.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain star fruit (carambola)?

rubric.true: The food contains star fruit or carambola juice.
rubric.false: The food contains no star fruit.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food a significant source of iodine?

rubric.true: The food is or contains seaweed/kelp/nori, iodized salt in notable amounts, dairy, egg yolk, seafood, or the colour erythrosine (Red No. 3).
rubric.false: The food is not a notable iodine source.

new_facets.jev_question: How good a source of iron is one typical serving?

levels: Poor.
Moderate.
Rich: about 20% DV (3.6 mg) or more, e.g., red meat, liver, mussels, fortified cereal, lentils, tofu, spinach (non-heme).

new_facets.jev_question: How good a source of calcium is one typical serving?

levels: Poor.
Moderate.
Rich: about 260 mg (20% DV) or more, e.g., milk, yogurt, cheese, fortified plant milk, calcium-set tofu, sardines with bones.

new_facets.jev_question: How protein-dense is this food per calorie?

levels: Low: under about 5 g protein per 100 kcal.
Moderate: about 5-10 g per 100 kcal.
High: over about 10 g per 100 kcal (e.g., chicken breast, fish, egg whites, Greek yogurt, tofu, cottage cheese, whey).

new_facets.jev_question: How energy-dense is this food (calories per gram)?

Medium: about 1.5-4 kcal/g.
High: over about 4 kcal/g (nuts, oils, chocolate, chips, pastries).

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain a nightshade vegetable or spice?

rubric.false: The food contains none of those; black pepper and sweet potato are false.

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food high in oxalate?

new_facets.jev_question: Is this food hard, tough, crunchy or sticky enough to be difficult to chew?

rubric.true: The food states <name> or a <name>-derived ingredient, carries a trace or cross-contact warning for <name>, OR lists a generic term that can legally hide <name> (e.g., 'spices', 'natural flavour(s)', 'seasoning', 'vegetable protein', 'starch') or has no ingredient list.

used_by: allergy_other_named (mustard, celery, lupin, corn, kiwi, coconut, buckwheat, sulfites...)
new_facets.note: Non-major allergens need not be declared and 'may contain' warnings are voluntary (FDA), so neither a Jev 'absent' nor a missing warning clears cross-contact. POLICY for a user-named (non-FALCPA) allergen: best possible verdict is 'unverified' ('No <name> in the ingredients; cross-contact is not declared by law'); a food becomes 'allowed' only when the user marks that exact product as checked (e.g., with the maker). Data class: to avoid a per-user question revealing a user's allergy to Jev, <name> must come from a GLOBAL list asked for every food (EU-14 + corn, coconut, kiwi, buckwheat, sulfites, mollusc, and names added by review). A name outside the global list is matched deterministically only, and the result stays 'unverified'.

new_facets.jev_question: Does this food contain <name> as an ingredient?

rubric.true: The food contains <name> or an obvious form of it.
rubric.false: The food contains no <name>; a flavour name without evidence of the ingredient is false.

new_facets.note: No cross-contact clause: dislikes and personal triggers are not allergies. Data class: the same global-list rule as contains_allergen applies; a user-specific name is matched deterministically in code and never sent to Jev as a per-user question.
